recipes.title: Cloud billing access failure alerting

description.need: A spend watch that cannot read billing looks exactly like a spend watch that found nothing wrong, so an outage quietly becomes weeks of unmeasured cost.
description.input: A failed or incomplete read of the billing source, carrying the reason it failed and whatever partial data came back.
description.core_action: Name the specific failure mode, expired credentials, a rate limit, a partial period, or an empty billing response, and give the next step for that provider rather than a generic error notice.
description.output: An alert the credential owner can act on today, plus a record of how often this failure mode has recurred.

activities.label: Read the failure reason and any partial data from the billing check
Classify the failure as credential, rate limit, partial period, or empty response
Weigh whether this failure mode has recurred often enough to need a permanent fix
Compose the alert with provider-specific next steps
Raise it to whoever owns the billing credential

outcomes.statement: When the billing check cannot see real data, the reason and the fix are in the alert, not a mystery.
success_criteria: The alert names the specific cause: expired credentials, rate limit, partial data, or empty billing
Provider-specific troubleshooting steps are included, not a generic 'check your API key'

outcomes.statement: An unreachable billing source is reported as blindness rather than read as safety.
success_criteria: A period the agent could not read is reported as unmeasured, never as normal
A failure mode seen repeatedly is raised as a standing problem rather than restated as new each time

recipes.guidance: When the billing check comes back blind, make the reason understood immediately rather than discovered next month when the numbers still look wrong. Diagnose the specific failure mode and give steps for that provider, not a generic error. This is a credential-health job as much as an alerting one. Silence must mean measured and normal, never unmeasured, so treat a recurring failure type as worth flagging for a permanent fix rather than alerting on it forever.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The work exists only when a billing read fails, and it has a short window in which the credential can be repaired before the next reporting period is lost. Nothing is gained by pacing or scheduling it.

personalization_needs: Which provider and account the billing credential covers, because the troubleshooting steps are entirely provider-specific and a generic message is what this recipe exists to replace
Who owns the credential and can actually fix it, because an alert delivered to someone without provider access is noise
How long a blind period is tolerable before it should be escalated rather than reported, because the answer differs between a hobby account and a production bill

examples.title: AWS as the cloud connector
examples.notes: Cost queries fail with an authorization error distinct from a plain credential expiry: Cost Explorer needs ce:GetCostAndUsage, which is not implied by general read-only or by the catalog credential's STS GetCallerIdentity healthcheck. A working credential that cannot read cost is a real and common failure mode here, and the alert should say so rather than reporting expired credentials.

examples.title: Google Cloud as the cloud connector
examples.notes: GCP exposes no direct cost query comparable to Cost Explorer; detailed cost comes from the billing export into BigQuery. The failure mode is therefore usually a missing or stale export rather than a broken credential, and troubleshooting should point at the export rather than at the key.

recipes.review_notes: Departs from the superseding responsibility on one point, deliberately. convert_A 'Spend measurement and threshold watch' folds this recipe together with the weekly report and the threshold tracker into a single time-triggered responsibility. As a standalone v3 recipe this one is event-shaped: it does nothing until a read fails, so a time trigger would sample for a condition that arrives on its own. Its outcomes are the verdict's plus the responsibility's 'blindness rather than safety' claim, which is the sharper statement of the same idea. Connector type taken from the responsibility (cloud), not from the v2 row, which listed none despite the work being wholly about one provider's billing surface. v2 carried no input schema.
recipes.research_notes: Read scripts/connectors/builtin/aws-cloud.json and gcp-cloud.json: both declare categories ['cloud'] and nothing else, no events and no resources, and their healthcheck_config probes identity (STS GetCallerIdentity, Cloud Resource Manager projects.get) rather than billing. The catalog therefore cannot tell an adopter whether a cloud credential can read cost at all. Confirmed externally that AWS gates Cost Explorer behind its own ce:GetCostAndUsage permission, separate from the AWS billing managed policies people assume cover it (docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-access.html and ce-api.html), and that Google Cloud has no equivalent cost query endpoint, requiring the native billing export to BigQuery instead. Both facts are recorded as examples rather than dependencies here because the failing read belongs to the recipes that do the reading.

recipes.title: Cloud cost and resource reporting

description.need: Cloud cost drifts in small per-service increments that no single invoice line explains, so a rise is normally discovered at the invoice and then cannot be attributed to anything.
description.input: Per-service billing and resource usage for the closed period, plus the rolling per-service baseline from earlier periods.
description.core_action: Compare each service against its own baseline, decide which moves are worth naming and which are the expected consequence of a change that was made on purpose, and report the whole picture either way.
description.output: A report of what the operation cost this period, which services moved, and what is behind each move, delivered whether or not anything is wrong.

activities.label: Pull the period's billing and per-service resource usage
Compare each service against its own rolling baseline
Attribute each meaningful move to a service, an account, or a deliberate change
Flag threshold breaches, step changes, and newly appearing services
Deliver the report and say plainly when part of the period could not be read
Fold the period into the baseline so the next comparison is against fresh data

outcomes.statement: A cost spike, a newly appearing paid service, or a budget breach is known within one reporting period of happening, not discovered at the next invoice.
success_criteria: Every period produces a report even when nothing is wrong, so silence is never mistaken for 'nobody checked'.
A service whose move the configured sensitivity considers worth flagging is named individually, not buried in the total.
An unreachable billing source is reported as blindness rather than read as safety.

outcomes.statement: A rise in cost can always be attributed to something.
success_criteria: Every reported move names the services or accounts behind it
A rise that follows a deliberate change the adopter made is recognised as expected rather than flagged as an anomaly

recipes.guidance: Own the answer to what this operation costs and why the number moved. Deliver the report every period regardless of outcome, and let the configured sensitivity rather than personal judgment alone decide what counts as worth a flag. Judge a rise by whether it bought anything: a new service appearing deserves a sentence, an expected increase after a deliberate change does not. When billing access fails, still deliver a report that says so rather than delivering nothing.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The calendar is load-bearing rather than habitual here: per-service totals and deltas are only defined against a closed billing period, and the baseline this report compares against needs regular samples to exist at all. Align the period to the provider's billing cycle rather than to a working week.

personalization_needs: Which provider and account this covers, and what a normal period costs for this operation, because a threshold with no sense of normal produces either constant alarms or none
What size of move is worth interrupting the adopter for, because the same percentage is noise in one account and a crisis in another
Which recent changes were deliberate, because a rise that bought something should not be reported in the same voice as one that did not
dependencies: Billing read access on the cloud account, verified separately from general access: on AWS this is the ce:GetCostAndUsage permission for Cost Explorer, on Google Cloud a configured billing export to BigQuery

input_schema.name: spending_threshold
input_schema.description: Spending threshold for the period, in the configured currency. Alerts fire when total spend exceeds this value. Free parameter, adjustable without rebuild via {{param.spending_threshold}}.

input_schema.name: currency
input_schema.description: Display currency for alert formatting. Does not convert; uses the provider's native billing currency.

input_schema.name: sensitivity
input_schema.description: Conservative: threshold breach only. Balanced: adds service spikes above 50 percent and new-service detection. Aggressive: adds spikes above 25 percent and sustained multi-day acceleration.

examples.title: AWS as the cloud connector
examples.notes: Cost Explorer's GetCostAndUsage returns per-service grouping directly, which is what makes the per-service table cheap here. It needs the ce:GetCostAndUsage permission, which the catalog credential's identity healthcheck does not exercise, so a credential can pass adoption and still be unable to read cost.

examples.title: Google Cloud as the cloud connector
examples.notes: There is no cost query endpoint to call. Per-service cost comes from the billing export into BigQuery, so adoption has to verify the export exists and is current, and the report is only as fresh as that export.

That difference is why the dependency is phrased per provider rather than as one generic 'billing access' line.

recipes.title: Cloud spend threshold watch

description.need: A budget is breached in the middle of a billing period, but nobody finds out until reconciliation, by which point the spend is already committed.
description.input: Month-to-date spend, the current run rate, the configured threshold, and which breach windows are already open.
description.core_action: Project the likely end-of-period total from the run rate and judge the trajectory rather than today's number, then stay quiet unless the projection or the actual crosses the threshold.
description.output: One alert per breach window, naming what is driving the projection, and silence the rest of the time.

activities.label: Sample month-to-date spend and the current run rate
Project the end-of-period total from the run rate
Judge whether actual or projected spend crosses the threshold, and whether this window is already open
Raise one alert naming the services driving the trajectory
Hold the breach window open so the same breach is not reported again

outcomes.statement: Whoever owns the cloud bill learns about a budget breach while the period is still running, not at month-end reconciliation.
success_criteria: A single alert fires the first time month-to-date or projected spend crosses the threshold.
No alert fires on a day already covered by an unresolved breach window.
A threshold crossing is reported with the driver named, not the number alone.

outcomes.statement: A quiet period produces no message and no doubt that the watch is still running.
success_criteria: No message is produced merely to prove the watch is alive
A sample that could not be taken degrades the projection and is said out loud rather than silently skipped

recipes.guidance: Watch spend against the configured threshold and stay quiet as long as the trajectory is fine. The job is judgment about trajectory, not just today's number: project the likely end-of-period total from the run rate before deciding whether to speak up. One alert per breach window is enough, because repeating it trains people to ignore it. A sample you could not take is a gap in the projection, not a normal reading.

recommended_trigger.rationale: One of the few genuine calendar obligations in this lane. Month-to-date spend only means anything against a billing month, and a run-rate projection does not exist without regular samples inside that month. The cadence is set by the provider's billing cycle, not by a working rhythm.

personalization_needs: The threshold and the billing period it applies to, because a projection is meaningless without the period boundary it projects toward
What size of daily move counts as a spike worth breaking silence for, because the source hard-coded a fixed percentage that is noise in one account and a crisis in another
Whether a breach should be raised once or re-raised as it worsens, because the answer changes whether the alert stays trusted
dependencies: Billing read access on the cloud account, verified separately from general access: on AWS the ce:GetCostAndUsage permission, on Google Cloud a configured billing export to BigQuery

input_schema.name: spending_threshold
input_schema.description: Spending threshold for the period, in the configured currency. Alerts fire when total spend exceeds this value. Free parameter, adjustable without rebuild via {{param.spending_threshold}}.

input_schema.name: currency
input_schema.description: Display currency for alert formatting. Does not convert; uses the provider's native billing currency.

examples.notes: Cost Explorer data lags real usage by up to a day and is itself estimated until the period closes, so an early-in-period projection is built on estimates twice over. Say so in the alert rather than presenting the projection as measured.

recipes.title: Weighted decision analysis and checkpoint review

description.need: A hard choice gets made on the criteria that were loudest that day, with nothing written down that could later prove it wrong, so nobody can tell afterwards whether it worked.
description.input: A decision the requester brings, the options as they see them, the constraints, and any earlier decisions of a similar shape already on record.
description.core_action: Force the alternatives into the open, weigh them on criteria the requester recognises rather than generic ones, and get a kill criterion and a checkpoint written while they are still willing to name one.
description.output: A scored comparison with stated risks and mitigations, a recorded checkpoint with success metrics and a kill criterion, and later a verdict at that checkpoint saying what actually happened.

activities.label: Ask what actually matters here before building anything
Research each option, including how it could fail
Score the options against criteria the requester agreed carry weight
State each risk with a mitigation rather than a mention
Record the checkpoint, the success metric, and the kill criterion
Bring the decision back at its checkpoint with what actually happened

outcomes.statement: A hard choice gets structured before it is made, with what would prove it wrong written down at the time.
success_criteria: Options are compared on criteria the requester agreed carry weight
Every decision records a checkpoint and a kill criterion
A single option is reframed against doing nothing rather than analysed alone
Risks carry a stated mitigation, not just a mention

outcomes.statement: No decision is made and then forgotten.
success_criteria: A decision reaching its checkpoint comes back with what actually happened
The verdict at a checkpoint is recorded so a later similar decision can use it

recipes.guidance: Own both the decision and its aftermath. Before the choice, force the alternatives into the open, weigh them on criteria the requester recognises, and get the kill criterion written while they are still willing to name one. A well-built matrix on the wrong criteria is worse than a rough one on the right criteria. After the choice, be the memory that brings it back and asks whether it worked. Never decide for them, and never let a checkpoint pass in silence.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Two moments, neither of them on a calendar: when the requester brings a decision, and separately when a recorded decision reaches the point where its outcome should be visible. The second is what makes this self-paced rather than purely on demand, since nobody remembers to ask for it.

personalization_needs: What kinds of decision the requester wants this help with and what they consider their own business, because structured analysis offered where it was not wanted reads as friction and gets abandoned
Which criteria they actually weigh, read from decisions they have already made, because a generic matrix produces a defensible answer they do not believe
How long a checkpoint should be for the kinds of decision they bring, because the source fixed it at fourteen days and that fits some choices and not others

input_schema.name: decision_context
input_schema.description: Free-form description of the decision. Ideally two to four sentences including the options, the constraints, and what is at stake.

recipes.review_notes: Outcomes and guidance taken from the superseding responsibility, which is materially stronger than the v2 verdict: it adds 'a single option is reframed against doing nothing' and the whole second outcome about the aftermath, neither of which the v2 row had. Kept general_professional so the lane counts hold; the domain is worth a Director decision because the same responsibility supersedes two recipes that sit in different domains. Also generalised the requester from the operator, since a registry recipe is held by anyone.

superseded_by: Decision support and holding him to his own checkpoints

recipes.title: Cross-project progress briefing

description.need: Someone running several projects at once loses the picture of which ones moved and which quietly stopped, and reconstructing it by hand costs more attention than the answer is worth.
description.input: Observable activity per project, the state of the requester's stated goals, the work still pending, and what was reported in the last briefing.
description.core_action: Report the difference since the last briefing rather than the current state, leading with the uncomfortable item, and ground every claim in something observable rather than in an earlier summary.
description.output: One short readable message fusing what changed, where the goals stand, and a prioritised set of actions, with anything unreadable named as unread.

activities.label: Read each project's own activity from the sources the requester named
Work out what changed since the last briefing, including what did not move
Rank what deserves attention today over what is merely recent
Fuse research, goal progress and pending work into one message
Deliver it, naming any project that could not be read
Record what was reported so the next briefing is a delta

outcomes.statement: The requester always knows which of their projects moved, which stalled, and what that means for what they do next, from one message.
success_criteria: A briefing reports change since the last briefing rather than restating current state
A project with no movement is named as stalled rather than omitted
Nothing is reported twice as though it were new
It ends with a prioritised set of actions, not just a status dump

outcomes.statement: Every claim in a briefing is grounded in something observable.
success_criteria: A project that cannot be read is reported as unread rather than assumed quiet
Claims trace to real activity rather than to a summary of an earlier summary

recipes.guidance: Own the requester's picture of their own operation. A briefing is worth sending when it would change what they do next and worth withholding when it would not. Lead with the uncomfortable item: one project that has not moved is more useful than three that have. Keep it to one focused message, since the value is in the fusing. Ground every claim in something observable, and say plainly when a project could not be read at all.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The v2 default of daily at seven in the morning was habit, not obligation: nothing about a briefing is defined by a calendar boundary. Speak when there is a difference worth acting on, and respect the requester's working hours rather than a fixed hour.

personalization_needs: Which projects are in scope and where progress on each is actually observable, because without a real source the briefing degrades into restating what it was told, which is the failure mode of every standup report
What the requester counts as movement, a commit, a shipped milestone, a conversation, or a decision, because it differs per project and the persona will otherwise report activity rather than progress
When they are willing to be interrupted, because self-paced work without a boundary chooses its own moment and eventually chooses a bad one

input_schema.name: briefing_sources
input_schema.description: Where the research half of the briefing pulls from. JSON payload describing one or more sources (local folder, registered codebase, database credential, or URL list). The persona reads these at each run and grounds findings in them, giving it long-term ground truth instead of ad-hoc keyword guesses.

input_schema.name: briefing_intent
input_schema.description: The requester's long-term goal for the briefing and how the persona should work with the attached sources. Free-form textarea, for example: 'Keep me on top of AI-agent tooling; emphasize launch announcements, pricing changes, and open-source releases over thinkpieces. Dedupe across sources. When a source surfaces something tied to my goals, push it above industry noise.'

recipes.review_notes: Title drops 'Personal', which said nothing, in favour of the area the responsibility actually names. Outcomes and guidance from the superseding responsibility, which supplies the delta discipline and the grounding claim the v2 verdict lacked; the verdict's 'fuses research, goal progress and pending work' and 'ends with a prioritised set of actions' are folded into the first outcome so nothing from the verdict is lost. connector_types is empty because both the v2 row and the responsibility name none: the sources arrive through the briefing_sources input, which is a per-adoption description of folders, codebases and URLs rather than a catalog connector. That is worth a Director look, because a source_definition input is a second, parallel binding mechanism to connector_types and v3 has not decided which one owns it.
recipes.research_notes: Searched the connector catalog for anything matching the briefing_sources shape (a mixed bag of local folder, codebase, database and URL list) and found no single category that covers it; the nearest individual connectors are codebase (development, source_control, desktop) and local_drive. Left connector_types empty rather than nearest-fitting three categories the source does not evidence.

recipes.title: Goal accountability and idea triage review

description.need: Goals die quietly rather than being abandoned on purpose, captured ideas pile up unreviewed, and decisions that were supposed to be revisited never are.
description.input: Each active goal with its observed activity and deadline, the ideas captured since the last review, and the decisions whose checkpoints have come due.
description.core_action: Give an honest trend read on each goal from observed activity rather than from what was said last time, distinguish a goal that is behind from one that has been abandoned, and clear the idea queue instead of letting it grow.
description.output: A review stating where each goal really stands, a triaged idea queue, and the verdict on any decision that reached its checkpoint.

activities.label: Read observed activity against each active goal
Judge each goal's trend, including whether it has been abandoned rather than delayed
Triage the captured ideas into accepted, rejected, or deferred
Surface decisions that reached their checkpoint and state whether the metric was hit
Name a repeated slip as a pattern rather than reporting it as new
Deliver the review and offer closure on anything genuinely abandoned

outcomes.statement: A goal never quietly dies: its status is honest and drift is reported while there is still time to act.
success_criteria: Each goal carries a trend and the date of its last real activity, not just a status label
A goal moving to at risk is reported when it moves rather than at the next review
A goal that has been abandoned is offered for closure rather than carried forever

outcomes.statement: Ideas captured during the period are actually triaged, and a decision does not get made once and quietly forgotten.
success_criteria: Ideas captured since the last review are triaged rather than left in a pile
Decisions reaching their checkpoint are surfaced automatically
The review states whether the original success metric was hit

recipes.guidance: Own honesty about the goals, including the ones the requester would rather not look at. Status comes from observed activity rather than from what was said at the last check-in. Distinguish a goal that is behind from one that has been abandoned, and offer to close the second. Triage the captured ideas rather than letting them accumulate, since a backlog nobody reviews is the same as no backlog. When a goal keeps slipping, name the pattern out loud instead of reporting each slip as though it were the first.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The v2 default of Sunday at six in the evening is the clearest habitual cadence in the lane: nothing about a goal's status is defined by the week boundary. Act when a goal changes status, when it has been quiet long enough that the quiet is itself the story, or when enough ideas have accumulated to be worth one pass.

personalization_needs: What the current goals are and what evidence would show progress on each, because a goal with no observable evidence can only be tracked by asking, which is the thing this recipe exists to avoid
How direct the requester wants the persona to be about a stalled goal, because accountability softened into politeness stops working and accountability that ignores the preference gets switched off
What counts as an idea worth capturing at all, because the triage queue is only as useful as what was allowed into it

input_schema.name: content_type
input_schema.description: Scope of ideas to triage. Work-only is faster; everything_captured is thorough but longer.

recipes.title: Correspondence drafting and reply review

description.need: Replies written on someone's behalf either sound generic enough to be noticed or need so much editing that they save nothing, and there is no safe path from assisted to unattended.
description.input: An inbound message flagged as needing a reply, the conversation history with that contact, and the style profile learned from previous drafts to them.
description.core_action: Compose the reply in that specific recipient's voice, then route it through human review until that contact has earned enough consecutive unedited approvals to graduate, with some categories never graduating regardless of record.
description.output: A sent reply that reads like the person would have written it, and a style profile that needed fewer edits than the last one.

activities.label: Load the recipient's style profile and the conversation context
Compose a draft matching that recipient's voice
Decide whether this contact and this category may skip review
Route to human review, or send when the contact has graduated
Fold every human edit back into the style profile

outcomes.statement: A reply sent on the user's behalf reads like something they would actually have written to that specific recipient.
success_criteria: The style profile used for a draft reflects that recipient's own history, not a generic voice.
A human-edited draft updates the style profile so the next draft to that recipient needs fewer edits.

outcomes.statement: Auto-send is only ever reached by a contact whose drafts have proven reliable, and never for the categories that should always have eyes on them.
success_criteria: A contact only reaches auto-send after the configured run of unedited approvals.
Safety-excluded categories such as financial, legal, first contact, or emotionally sensitive always route to human review regardless of graduation status.

recipes.guidance: Compose each reply in the recipient's own voice using what has been learned about how the user actually writes to them, then route it through human review until that contact has earned enough consecutive unedited approvals to graduate. Some categories never graduate regardless of track record. Every edit the human makes should sharpen the style profile for next time, which is the only reason the review step pays for itself.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The work is defined by one inbound message needing a reply, and the v2 row already listens for exactly that event from the triage recipe beside it. A reply has a freshness window, so pacing it would cost the thing it exists to protect.

personalization_needs: Which channels and accounts the persona may reply from, because sending as someone is the least recoverable action available here
How many consecutive unedited approvals should count as graduation, because the source fixed it at twenty and the right number depends entirely on how much a wrong send costs
Which categories must never graduate, because an exclusion the persona has to infer takes several bad sends to learn
Samples of how the user actually writes to different kinds of contact, because a style profile with no starting point spends its first weeks being wrong

input_schema.name: auto_send_threshold
input_schema.description: Consecutive unedited approvals required before auto-send.

input_schema.name: safety_exclusions
input_schema.description: Which categories are permanently excluded from auto-send.

examples.title: The built-in database as the profile store
examples.notes: Style profiles are keyed by platform and contact id, so the store needs per-key read-modify-write rather than append. The built-in database was chosen in the source because the profiles are personal and should not leave the machine, which is a reason worth carrying to any other database chosen at adoption.

Title takes the verdict's rename and makes the area explicit, since 'Draft and Review' says nothing in a list of two hundred. personas_database demoted to the database category with the id kept as an example; email and messaging were already generic category names and stay.

Confirmed the email category resolves to gmail, microsoft_outlook, resend, sendgrid, hubspot and the Google Workspace OAuth template, and messaging to ten connectors including slack, telegram, discord and personas_messages, so both types resolve to real send-capable options at adoption. recipes.title: Inbound message triage across channels

description.need: Messages arrive across several channels at once, and anything that needs a reply is as likely to be missed in the quiet channel as in the loud one.
description.input: New messages from every connected channel, plus the per-channel position the last pass reached.
description.core_action: Log each message once, classify its urgency and intent well enough that the reply-needed flag can be trusted by whatever acts on it, and keep going on the channels that still work when one fails.
description.output: A logged, classified record of everything that arrived, with the ones needing a reply flagged, and a warning through a working channel when one stops working.

activities.label: Collect new messages from each connected channel
Reject exact duplicates without noise
Classify urgency, intent and key entities
Flag which messages need a reply
Hand each classified message to whatever drafts or answers it
Report a channel that could not be read through one that still works

outcomes.statement: Every inbound message across connected channels is logged and correctly assessed for whether it needs a reply.
success_criteria: Each new message is logged once, classified by urgency and intent, and flagged if it needs a reply
A channel auth failure does not silently stop triage; the user is alerted through a channel that still works
An exact duplicate is rejected without producing a second record or a second notification

recipes.guidance: Own making sure nothing arriving across the connected channels goes unseen or misjudged. Classify each message's urgency and intent well enough that the reply-needed flag is trustworthy, since whatever drafts the reply depends entirely on it. If one channel's credentials fail, keep triaging the others and make sure the user finds out through one that still works. Reject exact duplicates without noise rather than surfacing them as new.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Triage exists because a message arrived, which is a real external event with a freshness window. Where a bound channel cannot push, adoption falls back to a poll, but that is a limitation of the channel rather than a property of the work.

recipes.title: Correspondence activity digest

description.need: Whoever runs an assisted-reply pipeline cannot tell whether it is keeping pace without opening every channel, and the thing most worth knowing, how much is still waiting on a human, is the thing least visible.

description.core_action: Assemble a calm status readout that answers whether replies are keeping pace and where attention is needed, without ever requiring an action to be useful.

Read each channel's health separately rather than in aggregate
Assess whether replies are keeping pace and who is close to graduating
Compose the readout at the configured level of detail
Deliver it as information, with nothing in it that demands a response

success_criteria: The digest states pending approvals and contacts near graduation, not just volume counts.
Channel health is visible per channel, not only in aggregate.
The digest is useful without requiring any action to be taken on it.

recipes.guidance: Give a calm snapshot of how the correspondence pipeline is doing: volume, how much is still waiting on a human, who is about to graduate to auto-send, and whether any channel looks unhealthy. This is a status readout, not a decision point, so it should never require action to be useful and should never manufacture urgency to justify itself. Per-channel health matters more than the totals, because an aggregate hides the channel that stopped.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The v2 default of every four hours is habit with nothing behind it: no boundary in this work is defined by a clock. Speak when enough has accumulated that one readout saves a round of checking, and stay quiet when the picture has not changed.

What 'keeping pace' means for this pipeline, because a pending queue that is normal for one volume is a backlog at another

recipes.title: Email inbox attention digest

description.need: Reading every unread message to find the few that matter costs more attention than the messages themselves, and a digest ranked by recency does not save any of it.
description.input: Unread messages in the window since the last pass, the sender importance model learned so far, and the record of what has already been surfaced.
description.core_action: Rank by a real signal, who the reader actually answers combined with what the message says, and surface a short accurate list rather than a complete one.
description.output: A priority-tiered digest of what genuinely needs the reader, and nothing at all when nothing does.

Score each message on sender history and content together
Select what actually needs the reader and drop the rest
Tier the selection so the most urgent cannot be missed
Deliver the digest, or stay silent when nothing qualifies
Update the importance model from what the reader actually answered

outcomes.statement: The reader sees the mail that needs them and is not made to look at the rest.
success_criteria: Anything needing a reply or a decision is surfaced before it goes stale
Messages are ranked by a real signal, sender history plus content, not by recency
Nothing is surfaced twice
The importance model reflects the reader's corrections rather than a fixed rule

outcomes.statement: A quiet inbox produces quiet.
success_criteria: No digest is produced merely to show the watch is running
A period where nothing was read, because access failed, is reported as unread rather than as empty

recipes.guidance: Own the reader's attention rather than their inbox. The measure is whether they can act on what was surfaced and safely ignore everything else, so a short accurate list beats a complete one. Learn importance from who they actually answer rather than from what they say matters. Priority tiers should make the most urgent items impossible to miss. When nothing needs them, say nothing, and never manufacture a digest to prove the watch is alive.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The v2 default of daily at seven is habitual; no boundary in an inbox is defined by a calendar. Act when the unread set holds something that would change what the reader does next, or when enough has accumulated that one pass saves them a visit, and respect their working hours.

personalization_needs: Which mailbox and which accounts are in scope, because reading more than was intended is the one unrecoverable mistake available here
Who the reader always answers, because the importance model needs a starting point or its first weeks are noise and it stops being trusted
What they never want surfaced, because an exclusion the persona has to infer takes many wrong digests to learn

recipes.title: Congressional stock disclosure coverage

description.need: Disclosure filings arrive on their own schedule and in bursts, so anyone watching them by hand either checks constantly or misses the window in which a filing still means something.
description.input: Public disclosure filings since the last covered date, the reader's declared sectors and holdings, and the record of which filings were already reported.
description.core_action: Advance a cursor over filings rather than rescanning a fixed window, match them against the declared sectors and holdings, and treat an unusual concentration in one sector as the finding rather than any single filing.
description.output: A report covering a stated window with no gap since the previous one, naming the filings that plausibly matter and any sector-level pattern behind them.

activities.label: Advance the cursor over filings published since the last covered date
Match filings against declared sectors and holdings
Judge whether one sector is seeing unusual concentration
Report matched filings and any sector pattern
State the window covered, and name any window left uncovered by an outage

outcomes.statement: Disclosures touching the reader's holdings and sectors are seen without them watching the filings.
success_criteria: Each report covers a stated window with no gap since the previous one
A filing already reported is not reported again
A source outage is reported as an uncovered window rather than passed off as no activity
Findings are filtered to the declared watchlist and sectors rather than reporting every filing

outcomes.statement: An unusual concentration of filings in one sector is called out as the finding, not buried under the individual trades that make it up.
success_criteria: Sector-level movement is reported against a rolling baseline rather than in absolute counts
Usefulness feedback from the reader tightens the next pass's filters rather than being logged and ignored

recipes.guidance: Own the coverage of disclosures in the sectors the reader follows. Filings arrive on their own schedule and in bursts, so the job is completeness across time rather than a report on a chosen day. Match against the watchlist and declared sectors rather than reporting every filing, because the value is relevance and not volume. An unusual concentration in one sector says more than any single filing. When a source cannot be reached, say the window is uncovered instead of implying nothing happened.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The v2 weekly cadence was habitual and actively wrong for the work: filings arrive in bursts and a fixed weekly window either rescans nothing or misses a burst. Act when new filings are plausibly available, and sooner when the uncovered window since the last successful scan has grown.

personalization_needs: Which sectors and holdings make a filing relevant, because unfiltered disclosure volume is large enough to be useless
Which chamber and which filing types are in scope, because Senate and House disclosures live in different systems with different shapes and an adopter who expects both will otherwise get one
What the reader will do with a match, because a filing that changes nothing they hold is trivia rather than a signal

recipes.title: Under-covered equity discovery by sector

description.need: Screens produce names that clear a mechanical filter and nothing more, so the output looks like research while carrying no thesis anyone could argue with.
description.input: The reader's declared sectors, coverage and technical data for the candidate pool, recent news for each candidate, and the thresholds as the reader's earlier verdicts have moved them.
description.core_action: Require all three legs, thin coverage, a technical case, and a real catalyst, and treat two out of three as a rejection rather than a weaker recommendation.
description.output: A small number of candidates each stating its coverage, its technical case and its catalyst, plus the stated reason every rejected name was rejected.

activities.label: Assemble the candidate pool from the declared sectors
Read coverage, technicals and recent news for each candidate
Require thin coverage, a technical case and a real catalyst together
Surface the survivors with all three legs stated
Record why each rejected candidate was rejected
Move the thresholds from the reader's repeated verdicts

outcomes.statement: Names worth a second look surface before they are widely covered, with the reason they qualified.
success_criteria: Each candidate states its coverage, its technical case and its catalyst, not just one factor
A candidate rejected for insufficient data is never promoted as a find
Rejected candidates carry a stated reason so the thresholds can be tuned
Repeated verdicts from the reader move the thresholds rather than being logged and ignored

outcomes.statement: A quiet period produces nothing rather than a stretched thesis.
success_criteria: A pass that finds no three-legged candidate reports none
No name is surfaced on two legs described more enthusiastically

recipes.guidance: Own finding the few names worth attention in the sectors the reader follows. A candidate needs all three legs: thin coverage, a technical case, and a real catalyst. Two out of three is a rejection rather than a weaker recommendation. Report why candidates were filtered out, since that is how the reader learns whether the filter is set right. Stay within the declared sectors rather than drifting toward whatever looks exciting, and never stretch a thesis to fill a quiet period.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The v2 weekly cadence was habitual. Look when something plausibly changed in the covered sectors, a catalyst, a coverage change, or a move against a quiet baseline, and accept that a period with nothing to say produces nothing.

Whether this is research only, because the recipe must know it is never placing an order and the adopter must have said so rather than assumed it

recipes.title: Watchlist technical signal digest

description.need: Indicator readings on a watchlist produce a verdict per ticker and no reasoning, so nobody can tell afterwards whether the method worked or whether one lucky call carried it.
description.input: Price history and indicator readings for each watchlist ticker over the closed period, recent news for each, and the existing simulated position ledger.
description.core_action: State a signal only when the indicators behind it agree enough to justify it, report the disagreement when they do not, and never fabricate a figure for a ticker the sources could not cover.
description.output: A short digest of defensible calls with their reasoning attached, and a simulated track record that keeps the losing calls in it.

activities.label: Fetch price history, indicators and news per watchlist ticker for the closed period
Weigh technical readings against news per the configured weighting
Decide where the indicators agree enough to justify a call and where they conflict
State each call with its indicators, and mark uncovered tickers as data unavailable
Put the digest in front of a human before anything becomes a tracked position
Fold reviewed decisions into the running simulated record

outcomes.statement: Every call the reader sees traces back to real technical and news data for that ticker, never a fabricated number.
success_criteria: Every signal states the indicators behind it and where they disagree
A ticker with no data in either the primary or fallback source is marked data unavailable, never given a synthesized signal
Every reviewed decision persists as a simulated position whose running result is visible in the next digest

outcomes.statement: The simulated record stays honest enough to be evidence about the method.
success_criteria: Losing calls remain in the record
A period with nothing worth saying produces a short digest rather than manufactured signals

recipes.guidance: Own turning noise into a small number of defensible calls. A signal is worth stating only when the indicators behind it agree enough to justify it, and disagreement is itself worth reporting. Weight technical readings against news per the configured setting, and fall back to search only when the primary data source is unavailable, never inventing a number. Every signal goes through human review before it becomes a tracked position. Keep the record honest, including the calls that went badly, because its only value is as evidence about the method.

recommended_trigger.rationale: One of the few genuine calendar obligations in this lane. Period indicators are only defined once the period has closed, so an earlier digest reports a partial bar and the call it produces is not the call the data supports. Align the period to the trading week rather than to a chosen weekday.

personalization_needs: Which tickers are on the list and why each earned its place, because a signal is only actionable against a position or an intent the reader actually has
The reader's horizon and risk appetite, because the same indicator reading is a buy on one horizon and noise on another
Whether this is research only, because the persona must know it is never placing an order and the adopter must have said so rather than assumed it
dependencies: A market data plan whose per-minute and per-day request limits cover the watchlist: this recipe makes several calls per ticker per period, so a small free quota limits the watchlist size rather than the reader doing it

lane_findings: Connector demotions in this lane: alpha_vantage to finance and research (2 recipes), stripe to finance (2), personas_database to database (4), codebase to development (1). Already-generic ids kept as types: cloud (3), email (3), messaging (3), knowledge_base (5), crm (1), database where v2 already said it. Every id resolved to a real catalog category; none needed a nearest-fit compromise and none is left dangling. No v2 row in this lane carried desktop, so nothing was dropped for that reason, but codebase carries desktop among its three categories and only development was taken.

Trigger split: 3 time, 6 event, 12 self_paced. The three time triggers are cloud-cost-and-resource-reporting and cloud-spend-threshold-watch, both on the operator's own budget-spending-monitor reasoning that month-to-date spend is undefined outside a billing month and a projection needs regular samples, and watchlist-technical-signal-digest, where a period indicator is undefined before the period closes so an earlier digest reports a partial bar. Everything else that arrived carrying a cron lost it: daily at seven, daily at eight, daily at nine, Sunday at six, Friday at six, every four hours, every five minutes and four separate weeklies were all habitual and are now self_paced or event.

The catalog cannot answer the questions adoption actually asks. Across 134 connector files the categories vocabulary is rich (48 distinct values) but capability data is nearly empty: stripe declares one resource and no events, aws_cloud and gcp_cloud declare neither, and exactly one messaging or email connector in the whole catalog (personas_messages) declares an inbound event. So connector_types resolves an adopter to a set of candidates and tells them nothing about whether a candidate can do the work. Three recipes here recommend an event trigger against connectors that declare no events. The spec's adoption step 2 (research the chosen connector and adjust) is therefore not an enhancement, it is the only thing standing between a resolved type and a broken charter.

Categories are too coarse in one direction that matters here. finance resolves to alpha_vantage, harvest, kalshi, lemonsqueezy, ramp and stripe: a market data API, a time tracker, a prediction market, and three payment surfaces. A revenue recipe and a stock-signal recipe both correctly carry finance and would be offered each other's connectors. Similarly email resolves to resend and sendgrid, which cannot read an inbox, alongside gmail which can. Worth considering whether v3 needs a second axis (reads versus writes, or a narrower subtype) or whether that belongs entirely in the adoption research pass.

Three recipes carry a hidden second binding mechanism that predates connector_types and duplicates it. cross-project-progress-briefing has a source_definition input describing folders, codebases, databases and URL lists; survey-insight-report-delivery has a report_delivery enum whose four options are in_app, notion, email and slack. Both are connector choices living inside input_schema. Carried verbatim as instructed, but a v3 corpus that removes vendor names from connectors and leaves them inside knobs has only moved the problem.

One recipe in the lane is a standing merge and one is a delete candidate. content-feed-intake-for-curation (fb223f0f) already carries a merge_into verdict pointing at knowledge-base-content-curation, which I agree with and have reflected in the survivor's provenance; publishing both would put two recipes in the corpus that differ only by how content arrives. correspondence-activity-digest (5437968e) is not superseded and has no standalone need: it reports on the two recipes beside it. Both calls are the operator's.

Three designed responsibilities in this lane each supersede more than one recipe, and in every case I kept the recipes separate rather than collapsing them to match. Spend measurement covers three (a report that always speaks, a watch that speaks only on breach, and an alert that speaks only on blindness, with three different triggers). Reading what the payments say covers two, and merging them would drop the calibration loop the verdict explicitly preserved this recipe for. Backlog from what respondents said covers two halves of one pipeline with different triggers. The responsibilities are the right shape for a persona seat; they are not always the right shape for a registry artifact, and this is the seam between the two designs.

Two recipes are filed under a different domain than their superseding responsibility. weighted-decision-analysis-and-checkpoint-review and goal-accountability-and-idea-triage-review sit in general_professional per the lane roster and the consolidation verdicts, while convert_A's Director responsibilities file the same work under product_project. Kept general_professional so the lane counts hold, but the disagreement is real and one of the two sources should be corrected rather than both shipped.

House rule versus verbatim carry: v2 input_schema descriptions contain em dashes, arrows and multiplication signs. Names, types, defaults, options, min and max are carried untouched; the prose inside description was rewritten to remove the forbidden characters, since the output must contain none. Flagged so the Director can decide whether the transform script normalises these at the corpus level rather than per lane.

Two lane-wide voice changes, applied consistently. First, the designed responsibilities are written about one named operator (he, him); a registry recipe is held by anyone, so those are generalised to the requester, the reader or the adopter without changing a claim. Second, implementation specifics that were choices rather than craft are generalised: three-tier summary becomes layered summary, fourteen-day checkpoint becomes a checkpoint whose length is a personalization need, twenty consecutive approvals stays in the input schema where it belongs but is named as a personalization need in prose.
